description: Brazilian proptech eliminating the 'fiador' (guarantor) requirement from rentals, using proprietary underwriting to insure landlords against tenant default. At Series D: the dominant rental marketplace in Brazil's largest cities, pre-bubble, expanding into home sales.
current_status: Largest proptech in LATAM at $5.1B valuation (unchanged since Aug 2021). Revenue >$150M in 2025. Shifted from growth-at-all-costs to profitability focus. Expanded from rentals into property sales. 3,000+ partner agencies. Active in 70+ Brazilian cities. ChatGPT integration for property search. No new funding rounds since 2021, operating on existing capital.

founder.name: Gabriel Braga + André Penha
founder.background: First-time founders, Stanford (CS/MBA). Strong technical backgrounds. Neither had operated in Brazilian real estate before founding.
founder.problem_fit: Personal pain (had trouble renting apartments in São Paulo) led to the insight — but the operational knowledge of Brazilian real-estate chains and guarantor culture had to be hired in.
founder.execution_evidence: Built the dominant proptech in Brazil's largest cities, acquired Casa Mineira, weathered the 2021 valuation reset without a down round.
founder.red_flags: No real-estate-industry co-founder; Loft has beaten them in São Paulo on listings supply — a warning that deep local operators still matter.

stage_context.vs_base: Expected thriving (+7pp) given rental-marketplace network effects and proprietary underwriting moat. Breakout (+3pp) reserved for scenarios where QuintoAndar becomes the de-facto embedded-mortgage origination layer for Brazil. Actual outcome landed one tier lower at surviving — post-2021 bubble adjustment plus Loft competitive pressure in São Paulo.

verdict: QuintoAndar survives IF (a) the underwriting model stays under 4% loss ratio through a full Brazilian credit cycle (untested — 2020-2022 had COVID moratoria), (b) home-sales business reaches breakeven by 2027, (c) Loft does not out-execute in São Paulo. Most fragile: (a) — the entire thesis rests on an underwriting model that has never seen a normal recession.
top_risk: Loss-ratio tail risk on the guarantor product: a single bad credit cycle could require R$500M+ in reserves the company does not have
top_opportunity: Embedded mortgage origination — QuintoAndar sees every qualified home-buying intent in Brazil first and can route it to lending partners for high-margin referral fees
actual_outcome: Thesis largely playing out. Rental business dominant and profitable; home-sales pivot underwhelming. Avoided a down round (unlike Kavak) but also not showing the EPS momentum a $5B valuation demands. Loft gained share in São Paulo per the risk note. Likely path: strategic acquirer (Itaú, Bradesco) or slow public listing; 10x Kaszek outcome looks unlikely — 3-5x more realistic.
